title: Maclaurin series: sin x built term by term
subject: math

scenes.caption: The constant polynomial matches only at 0
scenes.narration: The constant polynomial P equals 0 is a flat line. It touches sin x only at the origin, so it is accurate only at that single point.

shape.explain: Value axis: higher up means a larger value of the function.
x axis: further right means a larger x, with 0 at the centre.
Title: the constant polynomial matches sin x only at the origin.
Label: the vertical axis measures y.
Label: the horizontal axis measures x.
Target curve: the true sin x curve that every polynomial tries to match.
Constant term: with no x terms at all, the polynomial is 0 everywhere.
Approximation: watch it spread into the flat line P = 0, exact only where it crosses sin x at the origin.
Origin marker: the one point where P = 0 and sin x agree exactly.
Label: the flat polynomial is exact only at the origin.

steps.text: P = 0 matches sin x only at the origin - everywhere else the flat line misses the curve.

scenes.caption: Adding x: a narrow match near 0
scenes.narration: Adding the term x tilts the flat line into the diagonal y equals x. It hugs sin x near 0 but peels away beyond a narrow accurate region.

shape.explain: Value axis: higher up means a larger value of the function.
x axis: further right means a larger x, with 0 at the centre.

shape.explain: Title: adding the x term gives a narrow match near 0.

Approximation: watch it tilt from flat to the diagonal y = x, hugging sin x near 0 and peeling away beyond the band.
Accurate-region edge: inside the two green markers the diagonal stays close to sin x.

steps.text: y = x hugs sin x near 0, then peels away - the accurate region is a narrow band around 0.

scenes.caption: The cubic term widens the accurate region
scenes.narration: Subtracting x cubed over 3 factorial bends the diagonal into a cubic that follows sin x much further, so the accurate region around 0 visibly widens.

shape.explain: Value axis: higher up means a larger value of the function.
x axis: further right means a larger x, with 0 at the centre.

shape.text: Subtracting x cubed over 3!: the band widens
shape.explain: Title: the cubic term bends the line onto sin x and widens the band.

Cubic term: subtracting x cubed over 3 factorial bends the diagonal down onto sin x.
Approximation: watch it bend from the diagonal into a cubic, bending onto sin x over a wider band.
Accurate-region edge: the cubic stays close to sin x out to here, visibly wider than before.
Accurate-region edge: the cubic stays close to sin x out to here, visibly wider than before.
Label: the cubic is accurate over a visibly wider band around 0.

steps.text: The cubic term bends the line onto sin x - the accurate region around 0 visibly widens.

scenes.caption: The quintic matches widely, but not everywhere
scenes.narration: Adding x to the 5th over 5 factorial makes the polynomial near-coincident with sin x over a wide band, but far from 0 even the quintic diverges from sin x.

steps.text: More terms widen the accurate interval around 0 and improve accuracy there, but for any fixed polynomial the approximation still breaks down far from 0.
